key_insight: A polymorphic high-entropy oxide photocatalyst combined with microalgae as a sacrificial scavenger markedly boosts solar-driven CO2 conversion to CO and CH4 while adding a carbon-negative capture step.
engineering_relevance: The study points to a practical device-optimization strategy for improving photocatalytic CO2 reduction by tuning catalyst composition and using a renewable biological co-reactant instead of conventional sacrificial agents.
method: Designed an AB2O6-type high-entropy oxide, (Cs1/7Ba4/7Bi2/7)(Nb1/2Ta1/2)2O6, with layered perovskite/pyrochlore polymorphy.
Used Cs and Ba to raise surface basicity, Bi to promote polarization/charge separation, and Nb/Ta octahedra to support charge transport.
Compared CO2 conversion under three conditions: HEO alone, with microplastics, and with microalgae as the sacrificial agent.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that adding microalgae increases CO and CH4 production by about 10× and 4×, respectively, relative to the HEO-only system.
watch_item: The approach may face scalability and process-integration challenges, including maintaining stable microalgae handling and balancing biological CO2 capture with photocatalyst operation.
paper_title: Sustainable photocatalytic CO2 conversion using microalgae as a carbon-negative scavenger
